Add logic to clear this banner once `renderQueueTable` renders a non-empty queue. 10 11 ## Scope 12 13 - `mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js` — `renderQueueTable` function and/or `refreshQueue` flow 14 15 ## Deliverables 16 17 - Banner-clearing logic that removes the success banner from `#orch-preflight-results` after the queue table renders with at least one entry 18 - No change to the error banner behaviour (only the success banner is cleared) 19 20 ## Dependencies 21 22 - None 23 24 ## Acceptance Criteria 25 26 1. After launching an orchestrator run, the "Waiting for the run to appear in the queue below..." success banner is automatically cleared once the queue table renders with at least one entry. 27 2. Error banners in `#orch-preflight-results` are NOT cleared by this logic (only the success banner is affected). 28 3. If the queue is empty on refresh, the banner remains visible (it is only cleared on a non-empty render). 29 30 ## Active Pipeline Stages 31 32 `implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation` 33 34 ## Estimated Complexity 35 36 Low 37 38 ## Rationale 39 40 Clearing the banner on the first non-empty queue render is the simplest approach — no run ID tracking or cross-component state is needed. The edge case of a stale banner from a prior launch is acceptable since a page refresh resets it. 41 42 ## Rejected Approaches 43 44 - *Track launched run ID and match it in the queue* — Requires cross-component state (storing the launched ID and matching against queue entries). More complex for a marginal edge-case improvement. The simpler approach (clear on first non-empty render) is sufficient. 45 46 ## Notes 47 48 The success banner is written at line ~130 of `orchestrator.js` as a `

` inside `#orch-preflight-results`. The clearing logic should target this specific element/class to avoid accidentally clearing error banners. The banner-clearing code fits naturally inside the existing `renderQueueTable` function or immediately after its call in `refreshQueue`.

1	# WP-005: Expose `projectExists` flag and gate "View Project" button
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Polish the orchestrator GUI run queue view with five targeted fixes including hiding the "View Project" button until the project ledger actually exists.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Add a `projectExists: boolean` field to the `QueueEntry` interface and populate it in `getQueue()`, then update the frontend to gate the "View Project" button on this authoritative flag instead of inferring visibility from `effectiveStatus`. Include a unit test verifying the new field.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/types.ts` — extend `QueueEntry` interface
    14	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/get-queue.ts` — populate `projectExists` in the enriched result object
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js` — change "View Project" button condition
    16	- `mcp-server/tests/gui/queue/` — new or updated test file for `getQueue()` covering `projectExists`
    17	
    18	## Deliverables
    19	
    20	- `QueueEntry` interface includes `projectExists: boolean` field with JSDoc comment
    21	- `getQueue()` sets `projectExists` from the already-computed `projectStatus.exists` value (line ~155 of `get-queue.ts`)
    22	- "View Project" button rendered only when `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug` (replacing the current `status === 'started' && entry.expectedSlug` condition at line ~266 of `orchestrator.js`)
    23	- Unit test asserting `projectExists: true` when a ledger exists and `projectExists: false` when it does not
    24	
    25	## Dependencies
    26	
    27	- None
    28	
    29	## Acceptance Criteria
    30	
    31	1. The `QueueEntry` interface in `types.ts` includes a `projectExists: boolean` field.
    32	2. `getQueue()` populates `projectExists` from `projectStatus.exists` for every returned entry.
    33	3. The "View Project" button is NOT rendered when `projectExists` is `false`, even if `effectiveStatus === 'started'`.
    34	4. The "View Project" button IS rendered when `projectExists` is `true` and `entry.expectedSlug` is truthy.
    35	5. A unit test covers both the `projectExists: true` and `projectExists: false` cases for `getQueue()` output.
    36	6. Existing tests continue to pass without modification (no regressions).
    37	
    38	## Active Pipeline Stages
    39	
    40	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    41	
    42	## Estimated Complexity
    43	
    44	Medium
    45	
    46	## Rationale
    47	
    48	The backend already computes `projectStatus.exists` in `getQueue()` (destructured at line ~155) but does not include it in the response. Exposing it as a dedicated field is authoritative and zero-cost, avoiding heuristic guessing on the frontend. This follows the existing pattern of extending `QueueEntry` with computed fields (`effectiveStatus`, `progress`, `lastAction`, `logFilename`).
    49	
    50	## Rejected Approaches
    51	
    52	- *Infer from `effectiveStatus` alone* — `effectiveStatus` can transition to `'started'` before the ledger exists (when process is alive + has stage activity), producing a broken link. Not authoritative.
    53	- *Poll the project API from the frontend* — Adds an extra round-trip per queue entry per poll cycle for information the backend already has. Wasteful and racy.
    54	
    55	## Notes
    56	
    57	The `projectExists` value is already computed in `get-queue.ts` — this WP is primarily about threading it through the `QueueEntry` interface and updating the frontend condition. The backend change is a single line addition to the result object construction. No new `get-queue.test.ts` file currently exists — one must be created.

1	/**
     2	 * Shared type definitions and constants for the orchestrator run queue.
     3	 *
     4	 * This module is the leaf of the queue module dependency chain — it imports
     5	 * only from `compute-effective-status.ts` and has no other intra-queue
     6	 * dependencies.
     7	 *
     8	 * Dependency order (lowest to highest):
     9	 *   types.ts ← compute-effective-status.ts
    10	 *   format-progress-entry.ts  (independent leaf)
    11	 *   resolve-progress.ts ← format-progress-entry.ts
    12	 *   get-queue.ts ← types, resolve-progress, compute-effective-status
    13	 *   orchestrator-manager.ts ← get-queue, types, resolve-progress, compute-effective-status
    14	 */
    15	
    16	import type { EffectiveStatus } from './compute-effective-status.js';
    17	
    18	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19	// Constants
    20	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21	
    22	/** Filename of the shared run queue within the orchestrator logs directory. */
    23	export const QUEUE_FILENAME = '.run-queue.json';
    24	
    25	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    26	// Queue entry types
    27	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    28	
    29	/**
    30	 * Raw entry shape as written by the Python orchestrator to `.run-queue.json`.
    31	 * The `status` field is always `'pending'` at write time; effective lifecycle
    32	 * transitions are computed in-memory by `getQueue()`.
    33	 */
    34	export interface RawQueueEntry {
    35	  id: string;
    36	  pid: number;
    37	  planPath: string;
    38	  expectedSlug: string;
    39	  startedAt: string;
    40	  status: 'pending';
    41	}
    42	
    43	/**
    44	 * Queue entry enriched with computed lifecycle state and an optional
    45	 * human-readable JSONL progress summary. Returned by `getQueue()`.
    46	 *
    47	 * @remarks
    48	 * The fields that extend `RawQueueEntry` are all computed in-memory by
    49	 * `getQueue()` and are never persisted to the queue file:
    50	 *
    51	 * - `effectiveStatus` — derived from the PID alive-check, the presence of the
    52	 *   project ledger, and JSONL stage activity. See `computeEffectiveStatus()`.
    53	 * - `progress` / `lastAction` / `logFilename` — extracted from the most recent
    54	 *   JSONL log event by `resolveProgress()`.
    55	 * - `projectExists` — populated directly from `getProjectLedgerStatus().exists`.
    56	 *   Use this flag (rather than inferring from `effectiveStatus`) to gate UI
    57	 *   elements that require a valid project ledger, e.g. the "View Project" link.
    58	 */
    59	export interface QueueEntry extends RawQueueEntry {
    60	  /** Lifecycle state computed in-memory — not persisted to the queue file. */
    61	  effectiveStatus: EffectiveStatus;
    62	  /**
    63	   * Human-readable summary of the most recent meaningful JSONL log event,
    64	   * or `null` when no log file is found or no summarizable event exists.
    65	   */
    66	  progress: string | null;
    67	  /**
    68	   * The `action` field of the JSONL entry that produced `progress`,
    69	   * or `null` when `progress` is `null`.
    70	   *
    71	   * @remarks Callers can derive `hasStageActivity` from this field without
    72	   * reading the `ProgressResolution` object directly:
    73	   * `lastAction !== null && lastAction !== 'run_start'`.
    74	   */
    75	  lastAction: string | null;
    76	  /**
    77	   * Basename of the JSONL log file that was read, or `null` when no
    78	   * matching log file was found.
    79	   */
    80	  logFilename: string | null;
    81	  /**
    82	   * `true` when the project ledger file exists on disk for this entry's
    83	   * `expectedSlug`; `false` when it does not (e.g. the project has not been
    84	   * initialised yet). Use this flag to gate the "View Project" link — it is
    85	   * authoritative and avoids heuristic inference from `effectiveStatus`.
    86	   */
    87	  projectExists: boolean;
    88	}
    89	
    90	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    91	// Queue mutation types
    92	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    93	
    94	/**
    95	 * Result returned by {@link killQueueEntry}.
    96	 */
    97	export interface KillResult {
    98	  /** `true` when the entry was found, was effectively pending, and was terminated. */
    99	  killed: boolean;
   100	}
